page.layout: One column of letter text at top, ending with the signature line "Je suis à jamais". Below it, the greeting "Mon Pere," followed by two parallel blocks: left column the place and date ("De Greenwich, 5. de Juin, 1634."), right column the closing and signature. Then a centred heading "EPIST. XLVI.", a hanging-indent summary paragraph, an italic address line, the salutation "Mon R. Pere,", and a paragraph with a large initial. Catchword "com-" at the right foot. Page number and running head at the top.

main_text.p: Toute la Cour part d'ici pour aller au progrés dans cinq semaines au plus tard, & ainsi si vos lettres arrivent ici apres ce temps là, elles seront en danger d'estre perdues. Je suis à jamais
Vostre tres-humble & tres-affectionnée Ser-viteur R. Philippe P. de l'Or, de J.
main_text.head: EPIST. XLVI.
main_text.p: Philippus J. Morino. Quærit, utrum ve-rum sit, Canones Concilii Tridenti-ni, qui de Fide tractant, non recipi à Doctoribus Sorbonicis.

head.i: Au R. P. Morin, Prestre de l'Oratoire de Jesus.

page.notes: The final word of the page, "Pentateuche", is uncertain: the last letter may be a printed ę. The catchword "com-" is at the right foot. Long s is normalised to s throughout; the summary line "ve-rum" and "Tridenti-ni" are split across lines as printed.
